gameSystem.name: West Marches
gameSystem.description: A West Marches campaign for solo play, 5E compatible, on the SRD 5.2.1: a town, a roster of adventurers and one expedition per session, with rations, torches, abstract combat and encounters by distance. Original content: the flow, the tables and the sheet.

tags.label: Hireling
tags.hint: Hired help who may follow you out

tags.label: Patron
tags.hint: Someone who pays for the wilds to be explored

tags.label: Rival
tags.hint: A party after the same prize

trackers.name: Days away
trackers.hint: End the session in town, or the wilds keep you

trackers.name: Rations
trackers.hint: Each leg of travel eats one. At 0 someone goes hungry.

trackers.name: Torches burned
trackers.hint: Each room burns some light. A full clock means the last torch gutters.

trackers.name: Foe's hits
trackers.hint: Hits left before the foe falls

trackers.name: Threat
trackers.hint: How dangerous the fight is: it sets the damage you take

trackers.name: Expeditions
trackers.hint: Sessions spent on an expedition; the founding is not one

sceneTypes.name: Founding town
sceneTypes.purpose: Found the town the adventurers call home.
sceneTypes.tips: Think small: a village at the edge of the map with an inn and a notice board. The rumors you roll are the first reasons to leave it.

setup.title: What is it like?
setup.tip: A trade, a tavern, a lord, a smell.

sceneTypes.name: Roster
sceneTypes.purpose: Make the adventurers who might go out.
sceneTypes.tips: Make three adventurers now and up to two more. Every session sends a few of them out, so give them different classes. Build each on the sheet: roll abilities or spend the points, then set hit points and the kit.

setup.title: Who else stands out?
setup.tip: Someone who pays for the wilds to be explored, or who always wants more.

sceneTypes.name: Town
sceneTypes.purpose: Supply up, hire help and heal.
sceneTypes.tips: Spend the money you earned. Stock up on rations and torches, then visit the outfitter and the smith. Anyone with enough XP can level up.

setup.title: Does anyone offer to join you?
setup.tip: A hireling is an NPC who may follow you out.

play.title: Is anyone ready to level up?
play.tip: XP needed: level 2 at 300, 3 at 900, 4 at 2,700, 5 at 6,500, 6 at 14,000, 7 at 23,000, 8 at 34,000, 9 at 48,000 and 10 at 64,000. Raise Level on the sheet, then the maximum of Hit points and Hit dice.

play.title: Stock up on rations and torches?
play.tip: 5 rations and a fresh set of torches for 3 GP.

closing.title: Rest at the inn?
closing.tip: 1 GP buys a night of safe rest for one adventurer.

sceneTypes.name: Travel
sceneTypes.purpose: Cross the wilds toward your goal.
sceneTypes.tips: Each leg takes a day and a ration. The farther you go, the nastier the encounters. Getting back to town is its own scene: Return.

setup.title: Where to?
setup.tip: The next landmark, or a direction.

play.title: What do you see on the road?

closing.title: The rations are gone. Who goes hungry?
closing.tip: Exhaustion +1 for the adventurer you pick.

sceneTypes.name: Explore site
sceneTypes.purpose: Look over a place in the wilds.
sceneTypes.tips: Return to a known site, or find a new one and name it. It is kept as a Place near town, in the hills or deep in the wilds by how far out you are.

setup.title: Do you return to a known site?

play.title: Roll with…
play.tip: A test fits a search, a climb or a talk. Pick advantage or disadvantage by the situation.

play.title: Roll the test
play.tip: Pick the ability on the roll and set the DC.

play.title: Roll the test with advantage
play.tip: Pick the ability on the roll and set the DC.

play.title: Roll the test with disadvantage
play.tip: Pick the ability on the roll and set the DC.

sceneTypes.name: Delve
sceneTypes.purpose: Explore one room of a dungeon.
sceneTypes.tips: Each room burns a torch. A trap or a poison needle asks for a test, and a lair brings a fight. Add a room with Next room, or leave.

setup.title: A trap springs
setup.tip: Roll Dexterity in the mode that fits. A failure costs 2d6 hit points.

setup.title: A needle pricks the lock
setup.tip: Roll Constitution in the mode that fits. A failure costs 1d6 hit points and poisons you.

setup.title: The last torch gutters
setup.tip: Light another if you can, or press on in the dark: disadvantage on checks that need sight. Stock up in town to reset the clock.

play.title: What do you do in the room?

sceneTypes.name: Camp
sceneTypes.tips: Camping costs a ration and the night may be disturbed. Each adventurer rests in turn.

sceneTypes.name: Rest
sceneTypes.purpose: One adventurer takes a short or a long rest.
sceneTypes.tips: A short rest spends one hit die; an adventurer with none left takes a long rest instead. A long rest restores hit points, spell slots and half the hit dice, and removes a level of exhaustion.

play.title: Which rest?
play.tip: Choose an adventurer with each answer. Short rest needs a hit die: with none left, take a long rest.

play.title: Who recovers?
play.tip: Clears every condition of the adventurer you pick.

sceneTypes.name: Return
sceneTypes.tips: Getting home takes the rest of the day. The wilds let go of you.

sceneTypes.name: Encounter
sceneTypes.purpose: Meet someone or something on the way.
sceneTypes.tips: Decide what they want. A test settles a talk, and a fight is always an option.

setup.title: Who do you meet, and what do they want?
setup.tip: Use the Fate question when you do not know how they react.

play.title: Roll with…
play.tip: A social test or a read of the room. Pick advantage or disadvantage by the situation.

play.title: Roll the test
play.tip: Pick the ability on the roll and set the DC.

play.title: Roll the test with advantage
play.tip: Pick the ability on the roll and set the DC.

play.title: Roll the test with disadvantage
play.tip: Pick the ability on the roll and set the DC.

sceneTypes.name: Combat
sceneTypes.tips: Fights are abstract: the foe has a number of hits, and the threat sets the damage you take each round.

setup.title: Which monster do you face?
setup.tip: Name it as the encounter said, for example Goblin Warrior.

setup.title: How dangerous is it out here?

sceneTypes.name: Combat round
sceneTypes.tips: Each round: strike, then take the foe's blow. A spell uses a slot, and a potion heals in open play. Scenes of rounds repeat until the foe falls or you flee.

setup.title: Attack {fact:foe}
setup.tip: Roll melee, ranged or spell in the mode that fits and set the foe's Armor Class. A success is one hit.

setup.title: {fact:foe} strikes back
setup.tip: Set the foe's attack bonus, then roll. A hit costs threat × 4 hit points.

setup.title: Death saving throw?
setup.tip: Roll for an adventurer at 0 hit points. Three failures and it dies; three successes and it is stable (count them by hand).

play.title: Spend a spell slot?
play.tip: Pick the slot level of the spell you cast. Cantrips cost nothing.

play.title: Drink a Potion of Healing?
play.tip: Heals 2d4+2. Remove the potion from the pack by hand.

sceneTypes.name: Victory
sceneTypes.tips: Threat sets the reward: 10 GP and 100 XP at Minor, 20 GP and 400 XP at Tough, 30 GP and 900 XP at Deadly.

play.title: Who takes the spoils?
play.tip: Gold and XP go to the adventurer you pick.

flows.name: West Marches
flows.description: A town, a roster of adventurers and one expedition per session, with rations, torches and encounters by distance.
flows.introduction:
Solo play means you are the whole table: you describe what happens, roll the dice and make the calls. This guide gives you the questions so you can keep the story moving.

You play a West Marches campaign. First found the town and make a roster of adventurers; that is the first session. Then every session is one expedition: pick a rumor, choose who goes, travel out, explore and try to be back in town when the session ends. The farther you go, the nastier the encounters. Rations run low and torches burn down.

The rules come from the SRD 5.2.1: build your adventurers on the sheet, roll the d20 tests and fight with the abstract combat (the foe has a number of hits, the threat sets the damage). A few rules are hints, not automation: natural 20 criticals, conditions that give advantage, and the powers of your class.

phases.name: Founding
phases.description: Found the town and make the roster. Done when the roster scene ends.

phases.name: Expeditions
phases.description: One expedition per session. Done when you move on.

sessionOpening.title: Which rumor do you chase this session?
A fresh rumor reaches the inn. What is it?
sessionOpening.tip: Every thread is closed out, so a new one starts the expedition.

sessionOpening.title: Who joins this expedition?
sessionOpening.tip: Last session's party is still with you. Pick anyone new; whoever stays home is removed in the Party panel.

sessionOpening.title: Heading out
sessionOpening.tip: Starts the day count at zero.

sessionClosing.title: What happens out in the wilds?
Was this an expedition?
sessionClosing.tip: The founding session sets no expedition, so there is nothing to resolve.

worldTurn.title: Is a fight under way?
worldTurn.tip: A fight in progress is never replaced by a wandering monster.

worldTurn.title: Is a fight still being settled?
Does something find you?
worldTurn.tip: Roll 1d6. On a 1 the wilds answer.

worldTurn.title: What is in the deep wilds?

fields.label: Level
fields.hint: 1 to 10. Level up by hand: raise it, then raise the maximum of Hit points and Hit dice.

fields.label: XP
fields.hint: Victories add it. The town prompt lists the thresholds.

fields.label: Armor Class
fields.hint: Set it from your armor, shield and Dexterity.

fields.label: Hit die
fields.hint: The size of your class's hit die: 6, 8, 10 or 12.

fields.label: Exhaustion
fields.hint: Each level takes 2 from every d20 test. A long rest removes one.

fields.label: Conditions
fields.hint: Mark and clear them as they happen. Exhaustion has its own field.

fields.label: Spellcasting modifier
fields.hint: The modifier of your spellcasting ability.

fields.label: Level 1 slots
fields.hint: Set the maximum for your class and level. Leave it at 0 if you cast none.

fields.label: Gold
fields.hint: Gold pieces. Shops and inns take it.
